review.summary: AGENTLESS presents a deliberately non-agentic pipeline for repository-level issue resolution: hierarchical code localization, sampled diff-based repair, regression-test filtering, and majority-vote selection. On SWE-bench Lite, the authors report 82/300 issues resolved at an average cost of $0.34, and introduce a manually filtered 252-issue variant. The work offers a useful, interpretable baseline and component analysis, though broad claims about comparative performance are constrained by reliance on reported results for other systems and a single model/benchmark setup.

observations.claim: The paper gives a concrete and reproducible-in-principle pipeline, separating localization into file, code-element, and edit-location stages before repair.
observations.quote: AGENTLESS addresses this by using a simple three-step hierarchical localization process: 1) localize to selected files; 2) localize each selected files into relevant classes, functions, and variables; 3) localize to code edit locations.

observations.claim: The component results offer evidence that sampling/voting and test filtering improve the reported solve count over a single greedy patch, while also showing associated cost.
observations.quote: Starting with just generating a single sample (i.e., using greedy decoding), AGENTLESS can achieve 70 correct fixes while costing an average of$0.11 dollars per bug

observations.claim: Comparisons with prior systems are not uniformly controlled: several results are taken from external reports, and the paper notes that many systems' trajectories or source code are unavailable for verification.
observations.quote: For baseline tools, we directly use the reported results either from the official leaderboard [29] or from the tool’s official paper/repository.

observations.claim: The reported comparison does not establish how well the method generalizes beyond GPT-4o and SWE-bench Lite; the supplied evaluation specifies one implementation model and benchmark subset.

unresolved_questions: How robust are AGENTLESS's performance and cost results across other LLMs, model versions, repositories, and benchmarks?
How reproducible are the comparisons when all systems are run under the same evaluation setup, and how sensitive are results to benchmark or environment versions?

How consistent is the manual classification used to construct SWE-bench Lite-S across independent annotators? The inspected pages describe manual classification but do not provide an agreement measure.
Inspection was limited to the supplied text/pages; implementation details beyond the described setup and any supplementary analyses not included here were not assessed.
